rules.major_head: Health, Safety, and Essential Life Skills
rules.sub_activity_head: Emergency Response, First Aid, CPR & Fire Safety Training: Students who successfully complete a minimum half-day certified training programme in Emergency Response, First Aid, CPR, Basic Life Support (BLS), or Fire Safety shall be eligible for Activity Points. The training must be organized at the college level and conducted by Government organizations, approved training agencies, Fire & Rescue Services, or registered hospitals.
rules.documentary_evidence: Certificates must be issued by the Government organization, Fire & Rescue Services, approved training agencies, or registered hospitals. If unavailable, certificates signed by the faculty coordinator or the NSS Programme Officer may also be accepted.
rules.remarks: 5 Points /Training programme. Maximum-10 points shared with 1.21

rules.major_head: Health, Safety, and Essential Life Skills
rules.sub_activity_head: Activity Points for Students Who Know Basic Swimming
rules.documentary_evidence: Certificates issued by Panchayat/Municipality swimming instructors, Kerala State Sports Council coaches, or registered swimming academies. In the absence of the above, certificates issued by the institution’s Physical Education Department, based on a formally conducted swimming proficiency test, may also be accepted.

rules.sub_activity_head: English Proficiency Certifications
rules.documentary_evidence: Certificates issued by the official testing organizations or their authorized online portals. Students shall submit the original score report or downloadable digital scorecard issued by the respective testing authority. Only tests taken during the student’s original programme duration will be considered for Activity Points.

rules.sub_activity_head: Aptitude Proficiency Certifications (GRE, CAT, GMAT, GATE)
rules.documentary_evidence: Certificates / Score Reports issued by the official examination authorities or downloaded from the respective authorized portals. Students shall submit the official scorecard containing the score, percentile, test date, and candidate details.

rules.sub_activity_head: Industrial Visit /Industrial Training Report (S5 or S6): Students must prepare an Industrial Visit Report based on visits to a minimum of four industries relevant to their branch of study. The report should include key observations, processes studied, the major learning outcomes from each industry visited, and supporting photographs.
rules.documentary_evidence: The Industrial Visit / Industrial Training Report must be certified by the Faculty Coordinators / Faculty Members who accompanied the students for the visit, and by the SFA. The certification must confirm that the student has visited a minimum of four industries relevant to their branch of study and has submitted a report containing observations, processes studied, learning outcomes, and supporting photographs.

rules.sub_activity_head: Best Mini Project / Best Project / Best Seminar (from each class)
rules.documentary_evidence: The certificate must be issued by the Coordinator of the Project/Seminar evaluation Committee and the SFA and approved by the HoD. The certificate shall clearly state that the student has been selected for the Best Mini Project / Best Project / Best Seminar in the respective class, based on the department’s approved evaluation criteria.
rules.remarks: 5 Points. (To grant these points, the minimum class strength shall be 30 students.) Maximum- 20 points shared with 3.1

rules.sub_activity_head: Long-Term Internship: Internship for a minimum period of three and half months, as per KTU Long-Term Internship Guidelines
rules.documentary_evidence: Internship Completion Certificate mentioning start and end dates (minimum 3.5 months)

rules.documentary_evidence: Documentary evidence issued by the respective competent authority.

rules.sub_activity_head: Prototype Development & Testing: Development of a functional working model (hardware or software) that demonstrates the core functionality of an innovative idea. The prototype must be built, tested for basic performance, and validated by the Innovation Cell or other approved Government agencies
rules.documentary_evidence: Prototype validation certificate or letter issued by Government-approved innovation agencies.

rules.sub_activity_head: Innovative Technologies Adopted by Industry: Innovative hardware, software, or system solutions developed by the student that are formally adopted, implemented, or used by a reputed industry or organization. Adoption must be documented through an official letter, certification, or agreement issued by the industry or an authorized body.
rules.documentary_evidence: Official adoption letter / certification / MoU / implementation report issued by the industry or authorized organization.

rules.sub_activity_head: Venture Capital / Angel Funding – Receiving venture capital or angel investment for a student-developed product or idea, supported by official funding documents or agreements from the investor.
rules.documentary_evidence: Funding agreement, sanction letter, or investment confirmation issued by the angel investor or recognized funding body

rules.sub_activity_head: Societal Innovations - Innovative solutions, products, or technologies developed by students that directly address community needs or solve real-world social problems, implemented through IEDC, local bodies, or approved Government agencies. The solution must show measurable impact and be supported by a validation or appreciation letter from the concerned authority.
rules.documentary_evidence: Validation letter issued by IEDC / Local Bodies / Government Departments / NGOs / Approved agencies. Document must confirm implementation and measurable social impact of the innovation.

rules.sub_activity_head: Research Publication in Reputed Journals
rules.documentary_evidence: Paper copy or Acceptance Letter from the Editor/Editorial Office

rules.sub_activity_head: National Hackathons (Examples: Smart India Hackathon (SIH), KAVACH Cybersecurity Hackathon, hackathons organized by MoE, MHA, AICTE, Central Govt Departments, National Missions)
rules.documentary_evidence: Certificates issued by the Hackathon Organizing Authority
rules.remarks: Maximum- 40 points. No participation row in handbook.

rules.sub_activity_head: International Hackathons (Examples: NASA International Space Apps Challenge, Microsoft Imagine Cup, Google Solution Challenge, IBM Call for Code, Meta Global Hackathon, IEEE YESIST12 Global Finals, AWS Hackathons, Hack Zurich, Junction, etc.)
rules.documentary_evidence: Certificates issued by the Hackathon Organizing Authority
rules.remarks: 1. 1st Prize: 40 Points, 2. 2nd/3rd Prize: 35 Points, 3. Participation: 30 Points. Maximum- 40 points

rules.sub_activity_head: Skilling Certificates (Approved by the University): Courses offered by KTU with K-DISC, Government agencies, SWAYAM / NPTEL, Spoken Tutorial Project of IIT Bombay (recommended by BoS and approved by Academic Council)
rules.documentary_evidence: Certificates must be issued by the respective platform or organization, and the SFA shall ensure that the course appears in the University’s approved list of Skilling Courses and that the duration of each course is clearly indicated and meets the required hours before awarding Activity Points.
rules.remarks: 1 point per hour of approved skilling courses completed. Maximum- 40 points
